C.I.D. No. 2 Star Off XXXXX
November 26, 1921. S.
Student demonstration in New York in 1921.

C.D.I. Reeves.

Sir,

In June 1921 the Municipal Council passed
a resolution for the holding of Olympic Games to be held in the
New Park.

On June 4th 1921 while the Olympic Games were in progress
a large number of students who may be Chinese or socialists
carried banners carrying red, black, and white flags emblazoned
with violently worded political mottoes, others with
"Down with" and others with printed matter on them.
They paraded distributing leaflets causing a disturbance when
a pickpocket attempted to rob one of the public, he later
drew a pistol and fired several shots at him and others,
fortunately without causing casualties. The police succeeded in
arresting him and others including the principal. He
was sentenced to 3 years hard labour and expelled. Three
were sentenced to 6 months imprisonment each to be followed by
expulsion. Another was acquitted only on the ground that he
was under 16 years old. The incident shows that movements akin
to Bolshevism are slowly but steadily gaining ground in Shanghai
and other places and shows also the extent to which some of the
inhabitants in this city will go.

One of the slogans carried by these students is at present
in the C.I.D. Museum and copies of the leaflets in English
is attached. Copies and translations of the Chinese leaflets
are also attached (Municipal Budget for 1921 page 617).

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Percy A. Reeves
C. D. I.

D. C. I.

刑事调查处 第2星号官员 XXXXX
1921年11月26日。S.
1921年纽约学生示威事件。

刑事调查总监 里夫斯（Reeves）。

先生：

1921年6月，工部局通过一项决议，决定在新公园（New Park）举行奥林匹克运动会。

1921年6月4日，正值奥林匹克运动会进行期间，大批学生（可能是中国人或社会主义者）手持标语，上面绘有红、黑、白三色旗帜，并印有措辞激烈的政治口号；另一些标语上写着“打倒”字样，还有一些则印有印刷品内容。他们列队游行并散发传单，引发骚乱。其间，一名扒手企图抢劫一名公众成员，随后拔出手枪向他及其他人开了数枪，所幸未造成伤亡。警方成功逮捕了该扒手及其他人，包括主犯。主犯被判处三年苦役并驱逐出境。另有三人各被判处六个月监禁，期满后驱逐出境。另一人仅因未满16岁而被宣告无罪。此事件表明，类似布尔什维主义的运动在上海及其他地方正缓慢但稳步地蔓延，同时也显示了本市部分居民行事之极端程度。

这些学生所持标语之一目前存于刑事调查处博物馆，随函附上英文传单的副本。中文传单的副本及译文亦随函附上（参见《1921年度工部局预算》第617页）。

先生，
您顺从的仆人，
珀西·A·里夫斯（Percy A. Reeves）

September    25,    5.
Student Demonstration in Hongkew Park in 1921.

C.D.I. Reeves.

Sir,

In June 1921 the Shanghai Municipal Council granted
permission for the Far Eastern Olympic Games to be held in the
Hongkew Park.

On June 4th 1921 whilst the Olympic Games were in progress
a large number of students who may be classed as social extremists
entered the park carrying red, black, and white flags emblazoned
with violently worded anarchical mottoes, others with
"anarchist" and others with a pistol printed on them.
They started distributing leaflets advocating their views and when
an on-looker attempted to stop one of the youths, the latter
drew a pistol and fired several shots at him and others,
fortunately without harmful results. The police succeeded in
arresting six of the demonstrators including the ringleader. He
was sentenced to 10 years imprisonment and expelled. Three
were sentenced to 6 months imprisonment each to be followed by
expulsion. Another was released only and the case against the
sixth was dismissed. The incident shows that movements akin
to bolshevism were slowly but steadily gaining ground in Shanghai
and other places and shows also the extent to which some of the
enthusiasts in this work will go.

Some of the flags carried by these students are at present
in the C.I.D. Museum and copies of one of the leaflets in English
is attached Copies and translations of the Chinese leaflets
are also attached (see Municipal Budget for 1921 Page 61A).

I am, Sir,
Your obedient servant,
Percy S. Reeves.
C. D. I.

D. C. I.

1921年虹口公园学生示威事件。

C.I.D. Headquarter Staff      XXXXX
September    25,      5.

Extracts from the file on the 1915 Japanese Boycott and
the activities of the students in connection therewith.

C.D.I. Reeves.

Sir,
    In March 1915 a serious anti Japanese agitation was
brought about by certain Chinese who endeavoured to minister in
an open manner their prejudice against the demands made
against China by the Japanese Government.
    The first public signs appeared on March 7th 1915 and
a boycott on Japanese started on March 10th 1915.    The
banknotes of the Yokohama Specie Bank were refused by shop-
keepers and there was a run on the Bank.    Japanese sign-
boards were pulled down by the Chinese, rice merchants refused
to sell rice to Japanese and many Japanese were forced to
close their shops to protect themselves against violence.
On March 18th a serious attempt was made to incite popular
feeling against the Japanese.    A meeting was held in the
Chang Ya Ho Gardens.    Several thousands of Chinese
attended, but the majority of them were either returned
students from Japan or were attached to various colleges in
and around Shanghai.    It was remarked that not one single
respectable Chinese merchant having a stake in the place was
present.    Two men caused some excitement at the meeting by
writing certain characters in blood obtained by biting the
top of their fingers.
    In all cases where disturbance occurred the Police
found no difficulty in restoring order.    Several arrests
were made on charges of malicious damage to Japanese property,
and fines ranging from $1.00 to $100 were imposed.

摘自关于1915年抵制日货运动及学生相关活动的档案。

C.D.I. 里夫斯（Reeves）。

先生：
    1915年3月，一些中国人试图公开表达他们对日本政府向中国提出之要求的偏见，从而引发了一场严重的反日煽动活动。
    最初的公开迹象出现于1915年3月7日，抵制日货行动始于1915年3月10日。商家拒绝接受横滨正金银行的钞票，并发生了对该银行的挤兑。中国人拆除了日本人的招牌，米商拒绝向日本人出售大米，许多日本人被迫关闭店铺以保护自身免受暴力侵害。3月18日，有人企图严重煽动民众的反日情绪。在张园（Chang Ya Ho Gardens）举行了一次集会。数千名中国人参加，但其中大多数人或是从日本归国的留学生，或是隶属于上海及周边地区的各所学院。值得注意的是，没有任何一位在当地拥有产业的正派中国商人出席。会上，两名男子咬破指尖，用血书写某些字符，引起了一阵骚动。
    在所有发生骚乱的案件中，警方均能毫不费力地恢复秩序。数人因恶意破坏日本财产而被捕，并被处以1.00美元至100美元不等的罚款。

Extracts from the file on the 1919 Japanese boycott and
the activities of the Students in connection therewith.

C.P.I. Reeves.

Sir,

The anti Japanese agitation began in Shanghai on May
7th 1919. On that date a mass meeting attended by about
7000 people of whom the majority were students was held in
the Public Recreation Ground near the West Gate of the City.
Speakers demanded the return of Tsingtao and the release of
students who were imprisoned in Peking. After the speeches
the assembly decided to go in a body to see the Northern and
Southern Peace Delegates who were sitting at the German Club.
These plans were upset however by the French Police who would
not allow them to enter the Settlement. On the following
day thirty delegates representing as many educational
institutions met at the Fuh Tan College and formed a Students
Union. This organisation has since directed the boycott
campaign and had their headquarters at 51 Bubbling Well Road.
After June 9th it was located in French Town where they further
directed the boycott campaign. No violence took place until
May 18th when students and loafers began to snatch and
mutilate Japanese made straw hats.

The boycott was conducted in an orderly manner
despite the efforts of a few extremists among the students
who advocated the formation of a volunteer corps and a general
strike, but on June 4th the local Students Union received news
from their Tientsin branch that 400 students had been arrested
for demonstrating in Peking. On receipt of this report 300
students held a meeting in the Shanghai City. They formed

摘自关于1919年抵制日货运动及学生相关活动的档案。

C.P.I. 里夫斯（Reeves）。

先生：

反日骚动于1919年5月7日在上海开始。当日，在靠近城墙西门的公共游乐场举行了一次群众集会，约有7000人参加，其中大多数是学生。演讲者要求归还青岛，并释放被囚禁在北京的学生。演讲结束后，集会人群决定集体前往德国总会，去见正在那里开会的南北和平代表。然而，这些计划被法国巡捕打乱，他们不允许人群进入租界。次日，代表同样数量教育机构的三十名代表在复旦大学集会，成立了学生联合会。该组织此后一直指导抵制日货运动，其总部设在静安寺路51号。6月9日之后，总部迁至法租界，在那里继续指导抵制运动。直到5月18日才发生暴力事件，当时学生和游手好闲之徒开始抢夺并损毁日本制造的草帽。

尽管学生中少数极端分子主张组建志愿队并举行总罢工，但抵制运动仍有序进行。然而，6月4日，上海学生联合会从其天津分会获悉，有400名学生因在北京示威而被捕。收到此报告后，300名学生在上海城内举行集会。他们组成了

themselves into parties and made direct appeal to the City
shopkeepers to strike, with the result that on June 5th the
city shops did not open and those in the Settlement put up
their shutters. Japanese were attacked in various parts
of the Settlement during the day and at 9 p.m. large crowds
containing disorderly elements assembled on the Nanking Road.
Stones and bricks were thrown and several police injured and
at midnight it became necessary to disperse the crowds by
force. On June 6th reports were circulated that Japanese
were poisoning food and water, and a warning to shopkeepers
and others was accordingly issued by the Municipal Council.

On June 7th a meeting of representatives of various
trades, schools and associations held a meeting in the Nantao
Chamber of Commerce which was attended by General Lu. After
considerable discussion General Lu promised he would
telegraph to the Central Government urging the release of the
student demonstrators on the conditions that the shops would
open and the boycott agitation abandoned. These conditions
were opposed by the students and it had the effect of spurring
the students on to greater efforts and handbills were
circulated urging the people to continue the strike until the
Central Government agreed to the following demands :
1. The punishment of the National Traitors.
2. The cancellation of secret agreements.
3. The release of the students.
4. The return of Tsingtao.

他们结成党派，直接向市内店主呼吁罢工，导致6月5日全市商店未开门，租界内的商店也上了排门。当天，日本人在租界各处遭到袭击，晚上9点，包含不良分子的大群人群聚集在南京路。有人投掷石块和砖头，数名警察受伤，至午夜时分，不得不强行驱散人群。6月6日，流传着日本人正在食物和水中投毒的报告，工部局因此向店主及其他人士发布了警告。

6月7日，各行业、学校和协会的代表在南市商会举行会议，卢将军出席了会议。经过长时间讨论，卢将军承诺他将致电中央政府，敦促释放学生示威者，条件是商店开业并放弃抵制运动 agitation。这些条件遭到学生的反对，其效果是激励学生更加努力，并散发传单，呼吁民众继续罢工，直到中央政府同意以下要求：
1. 惩办国贼。
2. 废除秘密协定。
3. 释放学生。
4. 收回青岛。

Handbills were also circulated trying to undermine the
loyalty of the Chinese Members of the S.M.P. also to the
Soldier and Police in Chinese Territory.

The general strike continued to June 11th when news
reached Shanghai that the three so called National Traitors
had been dismissed by the President. On June 12th the shops
of the Settlement opened up and strikers began to resume work.
By June 16th things became normal.

The dismissal of the so called traitors was taken as
a victory for the people and celebrations started in Chinese
territory despite the orders of the Authorities.
Processions were formed and on one entering French Town it
was broken up by the Police. Part of it however entered
the Settlement at about 9 p.m. June 12th but was stopped by
the S.M.P. on Shantung Road. A fracas ensued and the Police
were attacked. The latter had to resort to the use of
firearms and several shots were fired which resulted in the
death of one Chinese and the wounding of several others.
There were few if any students in this procession which was
composed of commercial, citizens and other similar federations
accompanied by large numbers of bad characters from the City.

The reports that Japanese were poisoning the food and
water led to many grave assaults of Japanese and Koreans.
Many Chinese suffered also and two died from the wounds
received.

The strike showed that the Kohwingtong malcontents

第3页。

还散发了试图破坏上海公共租界警务处（S.M.P.）华籍警员以及中国领土内士兵和警察忠诚度的传单。

总罢工持续到6月11日，当时消息传到上海，称三名所谓的“国贼”已被总统免职。6月12日，租界内的商店开门，罢工者开始复工。到6月16日，局势恢复正常。

所谓“国贼”的免职被视为人民的胜利，尽管当局下达了命令，中国领土内仍开始了庆祝活动。组成了游行队伍，其中一支进入法租界时被警察驱散。然而，部分队伍在6月12日晚上9点左右进入租界，但在山东路被上海公共租界警务处（S.M.P.）拦阻。随后发生冲突，警察遭到攻击。后者不得不诉诸使用枪支，开了数枪，导致一名中国人死亡，多人受伤。这支游行队伍中几乎没有学生，它由商业团体、市民及其他类似联合会组成，并伴有大量来自市区的不良分子。

关于日本人正在食物和水中投毒的报告，导致了对日本人和朝鲜人的许多严重袭击。许多中国人也遭受了苦难，两人因受伤而死亡。

罢工表明，国民党不满分子

were responsible and in May 1919 a case occurred which disclosed the existence of a scheme to spread Bolshevist ideas in Chinese and that Bolshevik propaganda was being spread among the student classes and that agents for the sale of Bolshevik literature had been appointed in various schools. Books seized showed that agents had been appointed for their sale at schools as far apart as the Peking University - this is where the agitation started - and Lo Ying College near Swatow. Intercepted correspondence showed also that similar literature had been despatched to Chinese in England, France and America, and although there is nothing definite to connect Bolshevism with the unrest it is known that professional politicians and the student movement are closely connected.

So far as the students personally were concerned on this occasion few of them gave trouble in the streets. For the first day or two they were allowed to assist in keeping the crowds in order, but it was soon found that their presence merely caused larger crowds to collect. They were accordingly warned not to appear and they obeyed implicitly for some days. Later they formed processions carrying banners in motor cars and many had to be turned back. No students were arrested by the Police though a number found distributing handbills were take to Police Stations and warned to desist. On the whole they were amenably inclined and with few exceptions seemed anxious that order should be kept. No

对此负有责任，而在1919年5月发生了一起案件，揭露了在中国传播布尔什维克思想的阴谋存在，且布尔什维克宣传正在学生阶层中传播，并在各学校任命了销售布尔什维克文献的代理人。查获的书籍显示，远至北京大学——这是 agitation 开始的地方——和汕头附近的罗英学院（Lo Ying College，音译），都已任命了在学校销售的代理人。截获的信件还显示，类似的文献已被寄送给在英国、法国和美国的中国人，虽然没有任何确凿证据将布尔什维克主义与动荡联系起来，但众所周知，职业政客与学生运动有着密切的联系。

就学生个人而言，在这次事件中，他们在街头制造麻烦的很少。在第一两天，他们被允许协助维持人群秩序，但很快发现他们的存在仅仅导致更大的人群聚集。因此，他们被警告不要出现，他们在随后的几天里完全服从了警告。后来，他们组织游行队伍，乘坐汽车携带横幅，许多队伍不得不被折返。警方没有逮捕任何学生，尽管有一些被发现分发传单的学生被带到警察局并受到警告以停止此类行为。总体而言，他们倾向于顺从，除少数例外，似乎渴望维持秩序。没有

page_data.en:
Page 5.

cases of intimidation or of incitement by them to disorder
came directly under Police notice in Settlement limits.
When they started their boycott campaign they did not
intend the movement to reach the lengths it eventually did,
nor did they anticipate losing control as they did, but by
June 8th the conduct of affairs had admittedly passed out of
their hands and the attitude of their leaders on that day was
one almost of plaintive apology to the Police that things had
gone so far. They then stated that they were no longer
responsible for what might happen, giving as a reason that
there had been schism in their ranks and that they had no
authority over students who did not belong to their Union.
On June 6th 1919 the students of the Municipal Public
schools left the classes and walked out, necessitating the
closing of the schools.
On June 6th the president of the Students Union Ho Pao
Jien wrote to the Chairman of the Municipal Council stating
that the students were doing their best to maintain law and
order by having motor lorries travelling back and forth
bearing signs advising the people to be peaceful and quiet also
distributing handbills with the same object. He suggested
that interested parties would take steps to bring about a riot
and discredit the student movement and suggested calling out
the Specials and Volunteers. He expressed a desire to
to co-operate with foreign friends during the period of
internal dissention.

在租界范围内，警方直接注意到他们有任何恐吓或煽动骚乱的情况。当他们发起抵制运动时，他们并未打算让运动发展到最终那样的程度，也没有预料到会像那样失去控制，但到6月8日，事态的发展已公认超出了他们的掌控，那天他们的领导人对警方的态度几乎是带着哀怨的歉意，为事态发展到如此地步表示抱歉。他们随后声明，他们对可能发生的事情不再负责，理由是他们的队伍内部出现了分裂，且他们对不属于他们联合会的学生没有管辖权。1919年6月6日，市立公立学校的学生离开课堂出走，导致学校不得不关闭。
6月6日，学生会主席何保坚（Ho Pao Jien，音译）致信工部局总董，称学生们正尽力通过让载有劝告民众和平安静标语的汽车来回行驶，以及分发具有相同目的的传单，来维持法律和秩序。他建议有关方面会采取措施引发骚乱以抹黑学生运动，并建议召集特别警察和志愿队。他表示希望在内部纷争期间与外国朋友合作。

On June 7th 1919 Mr. Ho Pac Jien again wrote to the
Chairman expressing the Shanghai Students Union appreciation
of the tactful and useful conduct of the Volunteers. He
states "We feared that provocators would bring about a riot
to discredit our work for the Salvation of China. The co-
operation of the Volunteers and Student Groups saved the day."

On June 7th 1919 "The Students Union" issued a cir-
cular which reads as follows :-
"Your Country demands that you stay off the streets.
Go Home.
The enemy is trying to start a riot to damage our cause,
only peace and order can save China. If you are struck,
walk away. It will not be cowardice, it will be personal
sacrifice for your people "Go Home"

"Shanghai Students Union."

On June 10th 1919 another interesting letter was
written by Mr. Ho Poo Jien to the Chairman :-
"Sir,

It has come to the knowledge of the Shanghai Students
Union that the Municipal Council believes that the members of
the Union have participated in various strike activities to-
day, that they have intimidated shopkeepers to keep the shops
closed. Such information as you may have on this subject must
inaccurate.

The Shanghai Students Union has today been entirely
inactive. No members were on the streets participating in any

1919年6月7日，何柏坚（Ho Pac Jien，音译）先生再次致信总董，表达上海学生联合会对志愿队得体且有益的行为的赞赏。他称：“我们担心挑衅者会引发骚乱，以抹黑我们要拯救中国的努力。志愿队与学生团体的合作挽救了局面。”

1919年6月7日，“学生联合会”发布了一份通告，内容如下：
“你的国家要求你远离街道。
回家去。
敌人正试图引发骚乱以损害我们的事业，只有和平与秩序才能拯救中国。如果你被打，走开。这不是懦弱，而是为你人民的个人牺牲‘回家去’”

“上海学生联合会。”

1919年6月10日，何宝建（Ho Poo Jien，音译）先生给总董写了另一封有趣的信：
“先生，

上海学生联合会获悉，工部局认为联合会成员参与了今天的各种罢工活动，他们恐吓店主保持商店关闭。您在此事上可能掌握的任何信息必定是不准确的。

上海学生联合会今天完全处于不活动状态。没有成员在街上参与任何

agitation. It is quite possible that persons masquerading
as students have been going about town in order that the
students movement might be discredited. We are particularly
anxious to avoid any conflict with the Municipal Council; and
we are certain that you must recognize the fact that the
students have without delay complied with every order of your
body.

The Shanghai Students Union will be inactive tomorrow
except as the Council may wish to use its services. Should
any students be found disobeying the orders of the Council
will you be good enough to inform our Counsel, Mr. F.B. Rose,
of the fact so that it may be thoroughly investigated whether
the person is really a student who is endangering the move-
ment by disobeying our instructions or whether he is a fraud."

On June 11th 1919 the French Police gave notice to the
Public Citizens Association 220 Avenue Joffre and the Shanghai
Students Union 21 Yue Yong Lee Avenue Joffre, that they will
be obliged to leave the French Concession if the General
strike did not end on that day. As a result the students
on strike held a meeting in Muh Tan School for the purpose of
considering what should be done in view of their expulsion
from the International Settlement and their threatened
expulsion from French Town. They decided that they would
have no central organization until the general strike ended.

On June 11th 1919 while the City Magistrate and some
members of the committee of the Chinese of Commerce were

煽动活动。很有可能是伪装成学生的人在城里四处活动，以便抹黑学生运动。我们特别希望避免与工部局发生任何冲突；而且我们确信，您必须认识到这样一个事实，即学生们毫不拖延地遵守了贵机构的每一项命令。

除非理事会希望使用其服务，否则上海学生联合会明天将保持不活动状态。如果发现有任何学生不服从理事会的命令，能否请您告知我们的法律顾问F.B. Rose先生这一事实，以便彻底调查此人究竟是因违抗我们的指令而危及运动的真正学生，还是一个骗子。”

1919年6月11日，法国警察通知位于霞飞路220号的公共公民协会（Public Citizens Association）和位于霞飞路岳永里21号（Yue Yong Lee Avenue Joffre，音译）的上海学生联合会，如果总罢工不在当天结束，他们将被迫离开法租界。结果，罢工学生在慕尔堂学校（Muh Tan School，音译）举行会议，目的是考虑鉴于他们将被驱逐出国际租界以及面临被驱逐出法租界的威胁，应该采取什么行动。他们决定，在总罢工结束之前，他们将不设中央组织。

1919年6月11日，当上海县知事和华商公议会的一些委员正在

page_data.en:
Page 8.

holding a meeting in the room of the Chamber of Commerce on
N. Honan Road to consider steps to be taken to bring about a
resumption of business, a group of students entered the
meeting room and started to heckle those conferring. The
meeting broke up without reaching a decision.

On June 18th handbills purporting to come from the
Merchants Federation and Students' Association, which gave a
garbled account of the shooting affray on Nantung Road and
exhorting shopkeepers to strike again have appeared in the
Settlement. Neither of the organizations named are known
to the Police and it is believed that no such societies exist.

On June 16th 1919 an inauguration meeting of the
Chinese Students' Union was held in the Great Eastern Hotel,
Nanking Road, at 3 p.m. June 16. There were about 100
Chinese and eleven foreigners present. The former included
representatives of schools in Peking, Tientsin, Nanking,
Tsinanfu, Hupeh, Paotingfu, Anhwei, Kiukiang, Kirin, Tongshan,
Yangchow and Shanghai. With the exception of two newspaper
reporters, the foreigners who attended were American
missionaries or teachers in their schools. The gathering
was presided over by Tuan Sih Bang, a student in Peking
University.

Mr. Tuan started proceedings with a speech, in which
he explained the idea of the Chinese Students' Union, and the
reasons for its formation. He said the Union would try to
purge the Central Government of corrupt elements and would

河南北路商会的会议室举行会议，以考虑采取步骤恢复营业时，一群学生进入会议室，开始起哄那些正在商议的人。会议在未达成决定的情况下解散。

6月18日，声称来自商人联合会和学生协会的传单出现在租界，这些传单对南通路（Nantung Road，音译）的枪击事件进行了歪曲报道，并鼓动店主再次罢工。警方并不知晓上述两个组织，据信并不存在这样的社团。

1919年6月16日下午3点，中国学生联合会的成立大会在南京路东亚大酒店举行。约有100名中国人和11名外国人出席。前者包括来自北京、天津、南京、济南府、湖北、保定府、安徽、九江、吉林、唐山、扬州和上海的学校代表。除了两名新闻记者外，出席的外国人均为美国传教士或他们学校的教师。集会由北京大学学生段锡邦（Tuan Sih Bang，音译）主持。

段先生以一篇演讲开始了会议，解释了中国学生联合会的理念及其成立的原因。他说，联合会将试图清除中央政府中的腐败分子，并将

page_data.en:

strive for the regeneration of China. It would also use
all means at its disposal to protect China from external
enemies. The Union would have recourse only to peaceful
methods in carrying out its policy.

"Dear Monsieur Wilden,

It is reported that the Committee of the Public Citizens'

a meeting at which the organising of labour unions was the
principal topic discussed.

The Students Union moved into their new premises at No.
22 Rue Paul Beau on June 17.

It is reported that the Kuomintang intends to start a
weekly paper advocating Bolshevism. This journal will be
published in French town, and will be edited by the staff of

中国巡捕 456 号：昨晚约 8 时 55 分，我在爱德华七世大道（Avenue Edward VII）的电话亭执勤时，看见一百多名学生从法租界方向来到四川路桥附近。我在晚上 7 时上岗前曾被告知，不允许这些人进入租界。两名中国巡捕（62 号和 322 号）劝告他们不要进入租界。我看见中国巡捕正在与他们交谈。随后，他们沿着山东路转入中区。我随即通过电话向老闸捕房报告了此事。由于我留在警亭内，未再看到其他情况。

1919 年 6 月 12 日晚 9 时，我收到消息，称大批学生正经由山东路从法租界进入本租界。由骑警警长罗克（Sgt. Rock）率领的骑警队已被派出。抵达现场后，我看见骑警们正在进行激烈的搏斗。我看见一匹小马倒在地上，躺了几秒钟，

its rider was on the ground also stick, stone , and other

Among the debris we found a chopper. Crowds kept shouting

Trooper sergeant Rock.

I met a procession of Chinese dressed up in a way the
students have been dressing of late, white tops, little
cloth hats, long white gowns. They were carrying flags.
I rode up to a man who was leading the procession. I
addressed him in English as he spoke English well. I asked
him to go back to French Town and warned him that if he did

He spoke to the crowd and then said we will not go back. I

the activities of the students in connection therewith.
G.I.I. Reeves.

Sir,

The anti Japanese agitation began in Shanghai on May
7th 1919. On that date a mass meeting was attended by about
7000 people of whom the majority were students and was held in
the Public Recreation Ground near the race course of the City.
Speakers demanded the return of Shantung and the release of
students who were imprisoned in Peking. After the speeches
the assembly decided to go in a body to see the Northern and
Southern Peace delegates who were sitting at the German Club.
Their plans were upset however by the French police who would
not allow them to enter the settlement. On the following
day thirty delegates representing every educational
institution met at the Polytechnic College and formed a Students
Union. This organization at once directed the boycott
campaign from its headquarters at St Paul's; all road.
From June 9th it was conducted in French Town where they further
directed the boycott campaign. No violence took place until
May 18th when students and leaders began to snatch and
militate against made in Japan goods.

The boycott was conducted in an orderly manner
despite the effort of a few extremists among the students
who advocated the formation of a volunteer corps and a general
strike, but on June 4th the Students Union received news
from their friends in Peking that 400 students had been arrested
for demonstrating in Peking. On receipt of this report 300
students held a meeting in the Shanghai City. They formed

反日 agitation（煽动/骚动）于 1919 年 5 月 7 日在上海开始。当日，约有 7000 人参加了一次群众集会，其中大多数是学生，集会在靠近跑马厅的公共游乐场举行。演讲者要求归还山东并释放被囚禁在北京的学生。演讲结束后，集会人群决定集体去见正在德国总会开会的南北和平代表。然而，他们的计划被法国巡捕打乱，后者不允许他们进入法租界。次日，代表各教育机构的三十名代表在理工学堂（Polytechnic College）集会，成立了学生联合会。该组织立即从其位于圣保罗路（St Paul's Road）的总部指挥抵制运动。从 6 月 9 日起，抵制运动在法租界进行，他们在那里进一步指挥抵制运动。直到 5 月 18 日才发生暴力事件，当时学生和领导人开始抢夺并攻击日货。

the suburbs into order in the city of Shanghai, the merchants and shopkeepers of the City hoped that this would be settled without any further disturbance. These hopes were dashed in a short space of time when at about 9 p.m. large crowds containing mostly students assembled on the Nanking Road. Stones and bricks were thrown at several police officers and at midnight it became necessary to disperse the crowds by force. On June 6th reports were received that Japanese were poisoning food and water, and a warning to the shopkeepers and others was issued by the Municipal Council.

On the 7th a meeting of representatives of various bodies, including the Students' Union, held a meeting in the Nantao district of Shanghai which was attended by General Lu. After considerable discussion General Lu promised he would telegraph to the Central Government urging the release of the student demonstrators on the conditions that the shops would open and the boycott action abandoned. These conditions were opposed by the students and it had the effect of spurring the students on to greater efforts and handbills were circulated asking the people to continue the strike until the Central Government agreed to the following demands :

1. The punishment of the National Traitors.
2. The cancellation of secret agreements.
3. The release of the students.
4. The return of Tsingtao.

The strike which continued for over two months was finally
settled by the intervention of the authorities. On June 12th the
strikers returned to work under certain conditions which were
agreed upon by both parties. By June 16th the strike was over.

The strike was a victory for the people, and celebrations were held in the
territory despite the orders of the authorities.
Peace reigns were formed on one side and fighting broke out on the other.

firearms. Several shots were fired which resulted in the
killing of one man and the wounding of several others.

I was riding down the street, when I saw a large crowd of
Chinese being driven back by the police. I rode up to see what
was the matter. The mob had got possession of the street and
were throwing stones at the police. I drew my revolver and
fired three shots. The mob then fled 7 or 8 yards. I then
rode on. The crowd then came down again. I saw them shouting
"Down with the Foreigner". Our men opened fire on the mob in the
procession. I do not know how many were killed. I was in a
position to see what was going on. I saw one man shot through
the head. He fell dead suddenly like a stone.
TROOPER CHARLIE COCK.
I was at the corner of the road and saw a large crowd of
students coming down the road. They were carrying flags.
I rode up to a man who was leading the procession. I
asked him in Chinese if he spoke English well. I asked
him to go back to the Town and warned him that if he did
not there would be a possibility of some getting injured.
He spoke to the crowd and then said we will not go back. I
saw chairs and forms (stools) tables, cups etc. being thrown
from the windows. One trooper's jawbone was broken. I
heard them shouting "Beat the Foreigner". I fired 7 shots
from my pistol. The Volunteers turned out and relieved me.

警员查理·科克（CHARLIE COCK）。
我在路口，看见一大群学生沿路走来。他们手持旗帜。
我骑到一名带队的人面前。
我用中文问他英语是否讲得好。我要求他返回城内，并警告他如果不回去，可能会有人受伤。

我听见他们高喊“打外国人”。我用手枪开了7枪。万国商团出动接替了我。

Extracts from the File on the 1919 Japanese boycott and
the activities of the students in connection therewith.

C.D.I. Reeves.

Sir,

The anti Japanese agitation was started on May
7th 1919. On the 8th a mass meeting attended by about
7000 people of whom the majority were students was held in
the Public Recreation Ground near the east gate of the City.
Speakers demanded the return of Tsingtao and the release of
students who were imprisoned in Peking. After the speeches
the assembly decided to go in a body to see the Northern and
Southern Peace Delegates who were sitting at the German Club.
These plans were upset however by the French Police who would
not allow them to enter the Settlement. On the following
day thirty delegates representing as many educational
institutions met at the Fuh Tan College and formed a Students
Union. This organisation has since directed the boycott
campaign and has their headquarters at 51 Bubbling Well Road.
After June 9th it was located in French Town where they further
directed the boycott campaign. No violence took place until
May 18th when students and loafers began to snatch and
militate Japanese made straw hats.

The boycott was conducted in an orderly manner
despite the efforts of a few extremists among the students
who advocated the formation of a volunteer corps and a general
strike, but on June 4th the local Students Union received news
from their Tientsin branch that 400 students had been arrested
for demonstrating in Peking. On receipt of this report 300
students held a meeting in the Shanghai City. They formed

摘自关于1919年抵制日货运动及学生相关活动的档案摘录。

C.D.I. Reeves.

先生，

反日 agitation（骚动/运动）始于1919年5月7日。8日，在华界东门附近的公共游乐场举行了一次群众大会，约有7000人参加，其中大多数是学生。演讲者要求归还青岛并释放被囚禁在北京的学生。演讲结束后，集会决定集体去见正在德国总会开会的南北和平代表。然而，这些计划被法国警察打乱，他们不允许这些人进入租界。次日，代表同样数量教育机构的三十名代表在复旦大学集会，成立了学生联合会。该组织此后一直指导抵制运动，其总部设在静安寺路51号。6月9日之后，总部迁至法租界，在那里他们继续指导抵制运动。直到5月18日才发生暴力事件，当时学生和游手好闲之徒开始抢夺并毁坏日本制造的草帽。

尽管学生中少数极端分子主张组建志愿队和举行总罢工，但抵制运动总体上有序进行。然而，6月4日，当地学生联合会收到天津分会的消息，称400名学生因在北京示威而被捕。收到此报告后，300名学生在上海华界举行会议。他们组成

page_data.en:
Page 2.

themselves into parties and made a direct appeal to the City
shopkeepers to strike, with the result that on June 5th the
City shops did not open and those in the Settlement put up
their shutters. Japanese were attacked in various parts
of the Settlement during the day and at 9 p.m. large crowds
containing disorderly elements assembled on the Nanking Road.
Stones and bricks were thrown and several police injured and
at midnight it became necessary to disperse these crowds by
force. On June 6th reports were circulated that Japanese
were poisoning food and water, and a warning to shopkeepers
and others was accordingly issued by the Municipal Council.
On June 7th a meeting of representatives of various
trades, schools and associations held a meeting in the Chinese
Chamber of Commerce which was attended by General Lu. After
considerable discussion General Lu promised he would
telegraph to the Central Government urging the release of the
student demonstrators on the conditions that the shops would
open and the boycott agitation abandoned. These conditions
were opposed by the students and it had the effect of spurring
the students on to greater efforts and handbills were
circulated urging the people to continue the strike until the
Central Government agreed to the following demands :
1. The punishment of the National Traitors.
2. The cancellation of secret agreements.
3. The release of the students.
4. The return of Tsingtao.
page_data.zh:
第2页。

若干小组，直接向华界店主呼吁罢工，结果是6月5日华界商店未开门，租界内的商店也关上了排门。当天，日本人在租界各处遭到袭击，晚上9时，包含不良分子的大批人群聚集在南京路上。人们投掷石块和砖头，数名警察受伤，午夜时分，不得不武力驱散这些人群。6月6日，流传着日本人正在食物和水中投毒的报告，因此工部局向店主和其他人发布了警告。6月7日，各行业、学校和协会的代表在华人总商会举行会议，卢将军（General Lu）出席了会议。经过长时间讨论，卢将军承诺他将致电中央政府，敦促释放示威学生，条件是商店开业并放弃抵制运动。这些条件遭到学生的反对，这反而刺激学生更加努力地行动，他们散发传单，敦促民众继续罢工，直到中央政府同意以下要求：
1. 惩办国贼。
2. 废除秘密协定。
3. 释放学生。
4. 归还青岛。

page_data.en:
Page 3.

Pamphlets were also circulated trying to undermine the
loyalty of the Chinese Members of the S.M.P. due to the
higher pay police in Chinese territory.

The general strike continued to June 11th when news
reached Shanghai that the three so called strikers leaders
had been dismissed by the President. On June 12th the shops
of the settlement opened up and strikers began to resume work.
By June 16th things became normal.

The dismissal of the so called strikers was taken as
a victory for the people and celebrations started in Chinese
territory despite the orders of the authorities.
Processions were formed and on one entering French Town it
was broken up by the police. Part of it however entered
the Settlement at about 9 p.m. June 12th but was stopped by
the S.M.P. on Nanking Road. A fracas ensued and the police
were attacked. The latter had to resort to the use of
firearms and several shots were fired which resulted in the
death of one Chinese and the wounding of several others.
There were few if any students in this procession which was
composed of commercial, citizens and other similar federations
accompanied by large numbers of bad characters from the City.

The reports that Japanese were poisoning the food and
water led to many grave assaults of Japanese and Koreans.
Many Chinese suffered also and two died from the wounds
received.

The strike showed that the Kuomintang malcontents

还散发了小册子，试图因中国辖区警察薪资较高而破坏上海公共租界工部局警务处（S.M.P.）华籍警员的忠诚度。

总罢工持续至6月11日，当时消息传至上海，称三名所谓的罢工领袖已被总统免职。6月12日，租界内的商店开门营业，罢工者开始复工。到6月16日，局势恢复正常。

所谓罢工者的被免职被视为民众的胜利，尽管当局下达了命令，中国辖区内仍开始了庆祝活动。游行队伍组成后，其中一支进入法租界时被警察驱散。然而，部分队伍于6月12日晚9点左右进入租界，但在南京路被上海公共租界工部局警务处拦阻。随后发生骚乱，警察遭到攻击。警方不得不诉诸使用枪支，数声枪响导致一名中国人死亡，多人受伤。这支游行队伍中几乎没有什么学生，其成员由商界、市民及其他类似联合会组成，并伴有大量来自华界的不良分子。

有关日本人向食物和水中投毒的谣言，导致许多日本人和韩国人遭受严重袭击。许多中国人也受到伤害，其中两人因伤重不治身亡。

罢工表明，国民党不满分子

page_data.en:
Page 4.

were responsible and in May 1919 a case occurred which disclosed the existence of a scheme to spread Bolshevik ideas in Chinese and that Bolshevik propaganda was being spread among the student classes and that agents for the sale of Bolshevik literature had been appointed in various schools. Books sold showed that agents had been appointed for their sale at school, as far apart as the Peking University - this is where the agitation started - and Lo Ying College near Tientsin. Intercepted correspondence showed also that similar literature had been despatched to Chinese in England, France and America, and although there is nothing definite to connect Bolshevism with the unrest it is known that professional politicians and the student movement are closely connected.

So far as the students personally were concerned on this occasion few of them gave trouble in the streets. For the first day or two they were allowed to assist in keeping the crowds in order, but it was soon found that their presence merely caused larger crowds to collect. They were accordingly asked not to appear and they obeyed implicitly for some days. Later they formed processions carrying banners in motor cars and many had to be turned back. No students were arrested by the Police though a number found distributing handbills were taken to Police Stations and warned to desist. On the whole they were reasonably inclined and with few exceptions seemed anxious that order should be kept. No

第4页。

对此负有责任，且在1919年5月发生了一起案件，揭露了在中国传播布尔什维克思想的阴谋存在，显示布尔什维克宣传正在学生阶层中蔓延，且已在各所学校任命了销售布尔什维克文献的代理人。所售书籍显示，从 agitation（煽动/抗议活动）的发源地北京大学，到天津附近的洛英学院（Lo Ying College，音译），都已在学校任命了销售代理人。截获的信件还显示，类似的文献已被寄送给在英国、法国和美国的华人，虽然没有任何确凿证据将布尔什维主义与此次动荡直接联系起来，但众所周知，职业政客与学生运动之间有着密切的联系。

就学生个人而言，在此次事件中，他们在街头惹麻烦的寥寥无几。起初的一两天，他们被允许协助维持人群秩序，但很快发现他们的存在只会导致聚集更大的人群。因此，他们被要求不要露面，并在随后几天里完全服从。后来，他们组织游行队伍，乘坐汽车并携带横幅，许多队伍不得不被劝返。警方并未逮捕任何学生，尽管有一些分发传单的学生被带到警察局并受到警告，要求停止此类行为。总体而言，他们态度相当温和，除少数例外，似乎都渴望维持秩序。在租界范围内，警方未直接注意到

page_data.en:
Page 5.
cases of intimidation or of incitement by them to disorder
were directly under police notice in settlement limits.
When they started their boycott campaign they did not
intend the movement to reach the lengths it eventually did,
nor did they anticipate losing control as they did, but by
June 6th the conduct of affairs had admittedly passed out of
their hands and the attitude of their leaders on that day was
one almost of plaintive apology to the police that things had
gone so far. They then stated that they were no longer
responsible for what might happen, giving as reason that
there had been schism in their ranks and that they had no
authority over students who did not belong to their Union.
On June 6th 1919 the students of the Municipal Public
schools left the classes and walked out, necessitating the
closing of the schools.
On June 6th the president of the Students Union Ho Pao
Jien wrote to the Chairman of the Municipal Council stating
that the students were doing their best to maintain law and
order by having motor lorries travelling back and forth
bearing signs advising the people to be peaceful and quiet also
distributing handbills with the same object. He suggested
that interested parties would take steps to bring about a riot
and discredit the student movement and suggested calling out
the Specials and Volunteers. He expressed a desire to
to co-operate with foreign friends during the period of
internal dissention.
page_data.zh:
第5页。
有任何由他们进行的恐吓或煽动扰乱治安的案件。当他们发起抵制运动时，并未意图让运动发展到最终那样的程度，也未预料到会像后来那样失去控制，但到了6月6日，事态的发展显然已超出他们的掌控，当天其领导人的态度几乎是对警方表示哀怨的歉意，感叹事情竟发展至此地步。他们随后声明，对于可能发生的任何事情不再承担责任，理由是内部出现分裂，且他们对不属于其联合会的学生没有管辖权。1919年6月6日，市立公立学校的学生离开课堂出走，导致学校被迫关闭。
6月6日，学生会主席何保坚（Ho Pao Jien，音译）致信工部局董事会主席，称学生们正尽力通过派遣卡车往返行驶来维持法律与秩序，车上悬挂标语劝告民众保持和平与安静，并分发具有相同目的的传单。他建议，利益相关方可能会采取行动引发暴乱以抹黑学生运动，并建议出动特别警察（Specials）和义勇队（Volunteers）。他表示希望在内部纷争期间与外国友人合作。

operation of the Volunteers and Student Groups saved the day."

On June 7th 1919 "The Students Union" issued a cir-

"Your Country demands that you stay off the streets.
Go Home.
The enemy is trying to start a riot to damage our cause,
only peace and order can save China. If you are struck,
walk away. It will not be cowardice, it will be personal
sacrifice for your people "Go Home"
"Shanghai Students Union."

be

回家去。
